steps.label: Prompt
steps.text:
Make a 30-second launch film for [your product], 16:9 at 1920x1080, 30 fps.

Before you design anything, learn the product: read [your product URL], and the codebase if you have it. Write down in one line what it does and who it is for, list its three strongest features, and show me that summary first.

Story:
1. Hook, first second: one bold line or image that names the problem [your product] solves.
2. Meet the product: its real interface, logo, colours and type. No generic mockups.
3. Three beats, one per feature: show it working and give it one short line of copy, under eight words.
4. End card: logo, one-line promise and [your product URL].

Look and motion: calm and premium, like an Apple keynote film: lots of space, slow confident camera moves, one idea per shot, large type.

Use the product designs I give you as the source for every screen.
Pacing: measured, never frantic or bumpy. Hold each beat long enough to read, and move between beats with smooth, eased transitions.

Sound: use a royalty-free track (tell me where it is from) rather than composing one, and add subtle sound effects on the reveals. Mix so nothing clips.

How to build it: draw every frame in code as a pure function of time (HTML, Canvas or SVG, Remotion or HyperFrames all work), render the frames headlessly and assemble an MP4 with the audio. Then watch your render at full speed and fix anything that feels slow, cramped, generic or off-brand before you hand it over.

original.label: Prompt 1
original.text: Create a professional product launch video with motion graphics. You have access to the designs in pen

original.label: Follow-up
original.text: It is better, but can you choose a royalty-free song online? You are clearly not a good song maker. Also, I would not hire you or pay you for this as a motion designer. This is not a professional-looking video. Also, it is a bit too fast and bumpy
